problem: Object localization and object-goal navigation pipelines typically build dense 3D reconstructions (point clouds, voxel grids, scene graphs) that are slow to build, storage-heavy and hard to scale; zero-shot frontier methods avoid maps but must explore online and produce long paths.
motivation: In many robot settings (service, inspection, logistics) a prior RGB-D scan of the environment exists. VLMs and image retrieval models can reason directly on 2D observations, so the authors ask whether a dense 3D map is necessary at all for locating targets.
key_idea: Store only posed RGB-D keyframes as a visual memory, retrieve and VLM re-rank views at query time, then build a sparse on-demand 3D target estimate via segmentation, depth backprojection and multi-view fusion, with no global map.
insight: Reasoning over raw image memory can match or beat reconstruction-based pipelines, especially for fine-grained and image/language queries, while cutting preprocessing by orders of magnitude. Ablations show keyframe selection improves both SR and SPL over full frames (74.5→76.7 SR, 47.1→50.7 SPL) by removing redundancy, and images can be downsampled to 160x120 with only modest loss (SR 72.8). VLM re-ranking helps on fine-grained queries (HM3D +3.2 SR, real world 76→88%) but is not needed for broad category queries (MP3D unchanged SR).
method: Keyframe memory: select posed RGB-D keyframes when rotation >15° or translation >0.25 m from the last accepted one; store the images, depths and poses only
Stage 1 retrieval: SigLIP2 (SO400M) embeddings of keyframes indexed in FAISS; text, category or image queries retrieve top-K (K=10) by cosine similarity with dedup at 0.9

Stage 2 VLM re-ranking: Qwen2.5-VL-7B answers 'Is a {query} visible? yes/no <0-10>' per candidate; negatives are dropped and the rest re-ranked by score/10, with fallback to the best-scoring candidate
3D localization: SAM 3 text-prompted mask, discard views with median depth >4 m, backproject masked depth (0.1–20 m) to world coordinates into a sparse object cloud

Instance grouping and multi-view fusion: cluster predictions by overlap ≥15% or min distance <0.5 m; verify and fuse clouds from other/nearby views, clean with HDBSCAN largest cluster; the bbox centre is the goal
Navigation: pre-trained DD-PPO PointNav (VLFM config) with dynamic goal tracking to the closest visible cloud point, multi-goal fallback, and visibility-based STOP override

setting.backbone: SigLIP2 SO400M + Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (frozen) + SAM 3 + pre-trained DD-PPO PointNav policy
setting.observation: pre-scanned posed RGB-D keyframes plus egocentric depth at navigation time
setting.action_space: low-level discrete STOP / FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30°
setting.privileged: known camera poses for the pre-scan and the agent's pose/GPS-compass for PointNav; a prior RGB-D scan of the scene (pre-exploration)

numbers.extra: uses pre-scanned posed RGB-D keyframes of each scene; 1,000 episodes, delta=0.1 m
numbers.evidence: Table 2(a) Object goal navigation HM3D & MP3D: Ours 76.7 / 50.7

numbers.eval_set_note: GOAT-Core: 4 scenes (4ok, 5cd, Nfv, Tee), 480 subtasks; localization only, SR@5 with tau=1.5 m
numbers.extra: localization metric SR@5 (not navigation); pre-scanned posed RGB-D

numbers_note: GOAT-Core is localization SR@5, not navigation. Real-world Spot result (88.0% SR, 22/25 trials) is not a benchmark entry. ObjectNav splits are not explicitly named val in the text (HM3D v2 1,000 episodes assumed val).
results: On HM3D ObjectNav the method reaches 76.7 SR / 50.7 SPL, beating Uni-NaVid (73.7 SR) and VLFM's 30.4 SPL among frontier methods. On MP3D it gets 54.5 SR / 31.8 SPL (vs UniGoal 41.0 SR), and on HM3D-OVON val-unseen 52.5 SR / 38.2 SPL (vs MTU3D 40.8 / 12.1). Scene indexing takes 35.5 s and 1.4 GB vs 19.2 min for the next-fastest baseline (32x faster) and hours for HOV-SG.
limitations: Uses privileged pre-scanned posed RGB-D data and ground-truth poses, so it is not comparable to exploration-from-scratch methods and needs a prior scan
Per-query latency is high (2.92 s) because of VLM inference and segmentation; category-level queries are weaker than reconstruction-based LagMemo (79.5 vs 88.4 on GOAT-Core object goals)
Static scenes assumed; the paper's stated limitation on object-centric, single-view formulation is truncated in the text
